note: CI eval gates (spec §14; docs/eval-golden-set.md §6). EVERY number below is justified one by one in docs/eval/gate-model.md, which is the record, not this file. TWO layers, both ratchet UP only: `gates` are the aggregate floors, `per_language` the floors for every language the harness reports, so a weak language can no longer hide inside a healthy average (spec §14.3). A language the harness measures and this file does not name FAILS the gate check: an ungated language is the hole these floors close. Each floor is the HONEST CURRENT VALUE: the LOWEST value observed across EIGHT live runs of this exact prompt, corpus and model configuration on 2026-07-31, rounded down to two decimals of the TRUE fraction, never of the displayed percentage (54/73 prints as 74.0% and floors to 0.73, not 0.74). Never the specification target where the project sits below it, because a permanently red gate is not a gate, it teaches people to bypass it; and never inside a metric's run-to-run band, because a flaky gate gets ignored. No floor here was lowered: every aggregate floor is above the v1 value it replaces. Lowering one is a deliberate act that must be justified in the pull request that does it, with the measurement that justifies it.
chat_note: chat_gates: rule checks are all-must-pass in the harness; mean_coverage gates the MEAN of LLM-judged coverage across graded cases. Calibrated 2026-07-21 from the first temperature-0 baseline (mean 92.9% over 2 graded cases, atlas_scope 100 / who_is_ana 86): 0.65 leaves margin for residual provider nondeterminism on a small denominator while a broken prompt (historical degraded drill: single-digit coverage) lands far below. Ratchet UP only, same policy as gates.
